Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- Assessment consistent with Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) related to work stress (High likelihood); symptoms include anxiety onset after starting new job, irregular palpitations coinciding with anxiety episodes, sleep disturbance, low mood, social withdrawal, and decreased enjoyment in activities.  
- Possible depressive disorder (Moderate likelihood) suggested due to low mood and anhedonia but likely secondary or co-morbid with anxiety; no suicidal ideation or severe functional impairment reported.  
- Cardiac arrhythmia (Medium likelihood) considered due to irregular palpitations lasting minutes and associated chest discomfort; patient young with no prior cardiac history and symptoms closely linked to anxiety.  
- Hyperthyroidism (Medium likelihood) included as possible cause of palpitations and anxiety; no overt symptoms such as weight loss or tremor, to be excluded with planned lab tests.  
- Substance-related anxiety (Low likelihood) due to social alcohol use and occasional smoking which may contribute to symptoms.  
- No contradictions between transcript and DDx.  

Management Plan  
- Referral for one-to-one talking therapy/self-referral via NHS suggested; patient agreeable to therapy.  
- Provide online resources for immediate coping strategies while awaiting therapy.  
- Basic blood tests ordered to exclude medical causes (e.g., thyroid function, FBC, iron studies).  
- Follow-up GP appointment planned one week after blood tests to review results and reassess.  
- Advice on sleep hygiene to be provided.  
- Medication for anxiety not recommended initially but may be considered if symptoms worsen or do not improve.  
- Patient advised to contact healthcare provider urgently if symptoms worsen or daily functioning deteriorates.

- Generalized Anxiety Disorder (Work-related anxiety) – High likelihood  
  Justification: Symptom onset coinciding with new stressful job; classic anxiety symptoms including palpitations, sleep disturbance, and avoidance behavior.  
- Depressive disorder – Moderate likelihood  
  Justification: Low mood, anhedonia, decreased energy present; family history of depression; may be secondary or co-morbid with anxiety.  
- Cardiac arrhythmia – Medium likelihood  
  Justification: Irregular palpitations lasting 2-10 minutes; however, linked with anxiety episodes; no syncope or significant chest pain; young patient with no cardiac history.  
- Hyperthyroidism – Medium likelihood
